options.misconception: selects ‘thāʾ’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs
selects ‘nūn’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs
selects ‘ḍād’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs

questions.explanation: The sense ‘the trilled rāʾ’ is carried by ‘ر’. Apical trill, never a French r. The rival spellings each belong to a different item, so matching only the first letter or the general shape of the word will lead you astray.
questions.hint: Check every consonant of ‘ر’, not just its outline.

stimulus.body: قالت سارة: «قبل أن نبدأ، نحتاج إلى ____.» فقال عمر: «حسنًا، أحضرها الآن.»

questions.stem: In transcription, which form fills the blank for ‘lam’?

options.misconception: selects ‘thāʾ’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs
selects ‘ḍād’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs
selects ‘nūn’ whose written shape resembles the target but whose sense differs

questions.explanation: The blank is filled by ‘ل’, which means ‘the clear lām’ and fits the setting. Lateral approximant, light before vowels. The other forms belong to different items; choosing one would make the dialogue coherent in grammar but wrong in meaning.
questions.hint: Ask which meaning the situation calls for, then match the spelling.

questions.stem: In transcription, which claim about ‘nun’ is wrong?

options.misconception: treats a correct Latin rendering as the error
accepts a true spelling statement as the faulty claim
mistakes an accurate meaning for the unsupported statement

questions.explanation: The faulty claim assigns ‘the emphatic ṣād’ to ‘nūn’, but ‘nūn’ means ‘the dental nūn’. Nasal with dental contact. The spelling, the transliteration and the gloss are all accurate descriptions, so none of them can be the wrong statement the item asks for.
questions.hint: Find the statement that swaps in a meaning from a different item.
